seo.og_title: Toyota Harrier 2013-2026 Import from Japan NZ
seo.og_description: Looking at a Toyota Harrier 2013-2026? We help NZ buyers compare XU60 and XU80 model codes, grades, drivetrains and auction availability from Japan.

blocks.hero_subtitle: This is a good page to start with if you like the Harrier shape but want the facts straight before spending money. The 2013-2026 range covers XU60 and XU80 cars, with petrol, hybrid and later PHEV versions, so we confirm the exact model code, grade and listed equipment before any bid goes in.
proof_points: Importing estimate, with compliance as part of the process
blocks.why_kiwis_buy: The Harrier appeals because it sits between a mainstream medium SUV and a premium-badged alternative. The useful bit is that the range gives you real choice, early 2.0 petrol for simplicity, the 2.5 hybrid for lower running costs, or the later PHEV if you want a plug-in version within the Harrier range.
blocks.video_caption: If you are watching one at auction, pause on the rear badge area and interior shots. That is where we start separating a standard XU80 Z from a Z Leather Package or later Z PHEV, because the trim name alone in an ad is not enough.
blocks.main_usp_deep: The Harrier's main strength is breadth of choice across one familiar model line. XU60 covers the earlier 3ZR-FAE 2.0 petrol, the 2AR-FXE hybrid with 197PS system output and E-Four, and from the 2017 facelift the 8AR-FTS 2.0 turbo with a 6-speed automatic. XU80 moves to TNGA-K with the M20A-FKS 2.0 petrol and Direct Shift-CVT, the A25A-FXS 2.5 hybrid, and later the AXUP85 PHEV in Z grade. One useful thing many buyers miss is that a 2017-on XU60 turbo and a 2020-on XU80 petrol are not just different years, they are different platforms, different transmissions and different ownership propositions.

buyer_persona.headline: Who is this car right for?
buyer_persona.body: It suits someone who wants a medium SUV with a more upmarket cabin feel than a basic family wagon, but still wants Toyota running gear underneath. It also works for buyers who are happy to spend a bit more time choosing the right generation and grade, because the payoff is getting the drivetrain and trim that actually suits how you drive. If you want that mix of choice and clarity, this is a solid match.

car_specs_benefits.spec: XU60 production: Dec 2013 to May 2020, facelift from Jun 2017
car_specs_benefits.benefit: That split matters because the facelift adds the later turbo option and different grade ladder, so year alone does not tell you enough.

car_specs_benefits.spec: XU60 hybrid: 2AR-FXE 2.5L, 197PS system output, eCVT, E-Four AWD
car_specs_benefits.benefit: This is the earlier electrified Harrier for buyers who want hybrid efficiency and electric rear-axle traction without plugging in.

car_specs_benefits.spec: XU60 facelift turbo: 8AR-FTS 2.0L turbo, 6-speed automatic, FF or 4WD
car_specs_benefits.benefit: If you prefer a conventional automatic over an eCVT and want stronger mid-range pull, this is the XU60 to look for.

car_specs_benefits.spec: XU80 petrol: M20A-FKS 2.0L with Direct Shift-CVT
car_specs_benefits.benefit: The later petrol car sits on the newer TNGA-K platform, so it is the one to compare if you want the newer body and simpler non-hybrid running gear.

car_specs_benefits.spec: XU80 hybrid: A25A-FXS 2.5L with eCVT, FF or E-Four
car_specs_benefits.benefit: This gives you the newer-shape Harrier with the more modern hybrid setup, and E-Four is available if you want extra traction.

standout_features_block.headline: Features that stand out
standout_features_block.intro: The Harrier is worth separating by grade because some of the useful equipment sits in specific packages rather than across the whole range.

items.title: Leather Package grades
items.body: On XU80, G Leather Package and Z Leather Package sit above the standard G and Z grades. If leather trim matters to you, this is one of the easiest places to get caught by shortened NZ ad titles, so we confirm the original grade on the auction list rather than assuming from a seller heading.
items.image_hint: Front seats and centre console photographed clearly to show leather-trimmed seating surfaces and upper-grade cabin finish

items.title: Night Shade special editions
items.body: Later XU80 cars include Z Night Shade and Z Leather Package Night Shade editions. These matter because they are real factory special editions, not just a styling description added later, and they can change how a car is positioned in the market.
items.image_hint: Three-quarter exterior and cabin detail shots showing the special-edition trim treatment and grade-specific presentation

items.title: JBL audio on selected special editions
items.body: Toyota's special-edition listings confirm JBL branding on Night Shade equipment lists. For buyers who care about long-distance cabin use, branded audio is one of those details that is worth confirming on the exact car rather than assuming from the model name.
items.image_hint: Dashboard or door-speaker close-up with JBL branding visible beside the infotainment area

items.title: GR Sport and named package cars in XU60
items.body: The facelift XU60 range includes grades and packages such as Elegance GR Sport, Style Ash, Style Mauve, Style Noir, and the Metal and Leather Package cars. Those names are useful because they tell you the car sits outside the plain base-to-upper trim ladder, which can affect both equipment and buyer appeal.
items.image_hint: Exterior badge or interior trim detail that clearly identifies a package or special-edition Harrier

tech_deep_dive_block.headline: Under the skin
tech_deep_dive_block.intro: The Harrier story is really about how the platform and powertrain changed across the two generations.

items.title: XU60 range, 2013 to 2020
items.body: The third-generation XU60 runs from December 2013 to May 2020, with the facelift from June 2017. Early petrol cars use the 3ZR-FAE 2.0-litre with CVT in ZSU60W and ZSU65W model codes, while hybrid AVU65W cars use the 2AR-FXE 2.5-litre system with eCVT and E-Four. From the facelift, Toyota added the 8AR-FTS 2.0-litre turbo in ASU60W and ASU65W with a 6-speed automatic. That means a late XU60 can feel quite different from an early one even before you get into trim level.

items.title: XU80 range, 2020 to 2026
items.body: The fourth-generation XU80 starts from June 2020 and moves onto the TNGA-K platform. Petrol versions use the M20A-FKS 2.0-litre with Direct Shift-CVT in MXUA80 and MXUA85, while hybrid AXUH80 and AXUH85 cars use the A25A-FXS 2.5-litre with eCVT. Later in the range, AXUP85 brings in the PHEV version in Z grade. If you are cross-shopping years, this platform change is one of the biggest reasons to separate a 2020-on car from the older shape.

items.title: E-Four and the hybrid drivetrains
items.body: On the hybrid Harrier, E-Four is Toyota's electric AWD setup. Instead of a conventional mechanical link to the rear axle, it uses a separate rear electric drive arrangement to add traction when needed, which is handy on wet roads and loose surfaces. The XU60 hybrid is confirmed at 197PS system output, and the later XU80 hybrid continues the same broad idea with newer hardware.

models_comparison.intro: For the Harrier, the important comparison is not one badge against another, it is which generation and drivetrain you are actually buying.

rows.notes: Checked for the exact model code and vehicle before bidding, final certification occurs in NZ.

XU60: 3ZR-FAE 2.0 petrol CVT FF or 4WD, 8AR-FTS 2.0 turbo 6AT FF or 4WD, 2AR-FXE 2.5 hybrid eCVT E-Four. XU80: M20A-FKS 2.0 petrol Direct Shift-CVT FF or 4WD, A25A-FXS 2.5 hybrid eCVT FF or E-Four, AXUP85 PHEV E-Four.

XU60 moves from Grand, Elegance and Premium into facelift Progress, GR Sport and named package cars such as Metal and Leather. XU80 starts with S, G, G Leather Package, Z and Z Leather Package, then adds Z PHEV and Night Shade editions.
Availability changes a lot by generation and drivetrain. Plain petrol and hybrid cars give the broadest search pool, while special editions and PHEV cars need a more targeted search.

faq_block.q: What is the main thing to confirm on a Harrier before bidding?
faq_block.a: The model code and drivetrain. A Harrier ad title can hide the difference between XU60 and XU80, or between petrol, hybrid and PHEV versions, so we confirm that first from the auction information.

faq_block.q: What costs make up the importing estimate?
faq_block.a: We provide an importing estimate for the exact vehicle before bidding. Compliance and on-road costs stay separate and vary by vehicle.

faq_block.q: Can you tell me if a Harrier is typically within the entry requirements?
faq_block.a: Import viability must be checked for the exact model code and vehicle before bidding. Final certification occurs in NZ after the vehicle arrives and is assessed.

faq_block.q: How long does the process take?
faq_block.a: Timing depends on when the right car appears, whether your bid is successful, and shipping schedules after purchase. We keep you updated through the buying and arrival stages rather than guessing a fixed date up front.

faq_block.q: How do you help with auction condition information?
faq_block.a: We translate the auction list and explain the recorded grade, mileage, damage markings, condition notes and listed modifications. We also point out where the available information stops, so you know what is confirmed and what is not.

not_for_you_block.headline: Who this may not suit
items: If you want one simple trim ladder with no need to decode model codes, the Harrier can be more work than some medium SUVs.
If you need every infotainment and connected feature already set up for English use, confirm that on the exact car rather than assuming it from the grade.
If you only want the later PHEV, be prepared for a narrower search than standard petrol or hybrid Harriers.

battery_health_block.headline: PHEV battery and what we can confirm
battery_health_block.body: For a Harrier PHEV, battery-related information depends on what is supplied with that vehicle. We review the auction list, any supplied records and the listed warning status, then tell you what is confirmed and what is not.
checklist: Confirm the car is AXUP85 and listed as the PHEV version
Review any battery-related notes shown in the auction information
Check for warning lights or listed faults in the available records
Separate model-level PHEV facts from equipment confirmed on the exact car

charging_block.headline: Charging and daily use
charging_block.home_charging: The Harrier PHEV is the version for buyers who want a plug-in option within the range. Exact charging details need to be confirmed on the vehicle you are considering.
charging_block.public_charging: Public charging matters more if you want to use the PHEV regularly away from home. Exact charging-port details and charging speeds need to be confirmed on the vehicle you are considering.
caveats: Confirm charging details on the exact PHEV vehicle
Confirm any supplied battery-related records on the exact vehicle
Not every Harrier in this year range is a plug-in model
